Treasury Financing Operations
June Certificates and Bonds Refunded

On May 13, the Secretary of the Treasury announced that a new one-year 1-1/4 percent certificate of indebtedness would be offered to holders of the Treasury 1-1/8 percent certificates of indebtedness, Series E-1949, maturing June 1, 1949, and to holders of the 2 percent Treasury bonds of 1949-51, dated January 15, 1942, which had been called on February 14 for redemption on June 15. The maturing certificates totaled $4,301 million and the called bonds totaled $1,014 million.

Subscription books for the exchange offering were opened May 19 and were closed at the close of business May 23. The new certificates, Series E-1950, were dated June 1, 1949, and bear interest from that date at the rate of 1-1/4 percent per annum, payable with the principal at maturity on June 1, 1950.

Exchanges were made par for par in respect to the maturing certificates, and at par with an adjustment for interest as of June 15, 1949, in the case of the called bonds. Cash subscriptions were not received. The new certificates were issued in bearer form only, in denominations of $1,000, $5,000, $10,000, $100,000 and $1,000,000.
Reports to the Treasury on the ownership of Government securities indicate that on March 31, 1949, about 54 percent of the maturing certificates

and about 66 percent of the called bonds were owned by reporting commercial banks and Federal Reserve Banks. The ownership figures for March 31 are the latest available for holdings of commercial banks.
Subscriptions to the new certificates amounted to $5,018 million on the basis of preliminary figures, leaving $297 million of the two maturing issues to be paid in cash.
Call of 2 Percent Treasury Bonds of 1949- 51 (September)

On May 13, the Secretary announced that all outstanding 2 percent Treasury bonds of 1949-51 dated May 15, 1942, are called for redemption on September 15, 1949. The amount of this issue outstanding is $1,292 million. The announcement stated that holders of these bonds, in advance of the redemption date, may be offered the privilege of exchanging all or part of their called bonds for other interest-bearing obligations of the United States, in which event public notice will hereafter be given.
Treasury Bills Refunded

Treasury bills maturing in May were refunded in the full amount of $3.4 billion. The issues dated May 5 and 19 totaled $800 million each and those of May 12 and 26 totaled $900 million each. The successive average rates of discount on the four issues were 1.147 percent, 1.148 percent, 1.157 percent, and 1.159 percent.

CAPITAL MOVEMENTS

Information relating to capital movements between the United States and foreign countries is presented in four sections. Section I presents first a historical summary of the principal types of data on capital movements, beginning with 1935 when the information was first compiled. Each type of data is then broken down into its chief components in the same chronological detail.

Section II supplies a geographic breakdown by principal countries for recent months. The total net capital movement is given first and then the principal categories are shown separately. In addition, at this point, the total outstanding claims on and liabilities to foreign countries are each presented.
Section III presents details with respect to capital movements and short-term claims and liabilities. These are shown for the latest month for which final data are
available and the latest month for which preliminary data are available.
Section IV contains data for recent months on outstanding contracts of banks for forward purchases and sales of foreign exchange.

The data in these four sections are based on reports filed each month by banks, bankers, and brokers throughout the United States. The reports are collected, checked, and tabulated by the twelve Federal Reserve Banks. The totals are then forwarded to the Treasury Department for consolidation and publication.

Publication of detailed figures on capital movements was discontinued between the March 1942 and the November 1945 issues of the "Treasury Bulletin", but data omitted during that period were supplied in the November 1945 issue and supplement.
